title: Course 1 Synthetic Traceability and Reconciliation Exercise
description: Synthetic instructional records for practicing identity preservation, movement-event reconstruction, physical-versus-record reconciliation, discrepancy handling, and shift handoff. The records do not describe a real facility, crop, person, or regulatory system.

fields.timestamp: Synthetic event time in ISO 8601 format
fields.eventType: Receive, move, split, hold, count, reconcile, or handoff
fields.sourceLocation: Location before the event when applicable
fields.destinationLocation: Location after the event when applicable
fields.quantity: Synthetic count associated with the event
fields.notes: Factual event context; may intentionally contain an unresolved discrepancy for learner analysis

events.notes: Intake identity and count confirmed at receipt.
Movement completed under work order WO-1001.
Eight units retained under source identity; four units assigned child identity LOT-A100-S1.
Child identity created from LOT-A100 and moved to ROOM-C.
Hold applied pending identity review; no movement authorized while hold remains active.
Physical count agrees with post-split record.
Physical count is three while the recorded split quantity is four; discrepancy remains unresolved.
No adjustment made. Physical count, recorded quantity, hold status, and discrepancy are preserved for authorized investigation.
Incoming shift receives exact object ID, physical count, recorded count, active hold, open discrepancy, and next review action.

learnerTasks: Reconstruct the event genealogy for LOT-A100 and LOT-A100-S1.
Identify the first event at which the child identity exists.
Compare the recorded and physical states for both identities.
Identify which work remains blocked by the active hold.
Describe what must remain unresolved rather than being silently corrected.
Prepare a factual handoff containing identity, location, status, discrepancy, actions already taken, and next authorized action.
